ai.description: This snake reaches 1 meter in length. It is dark grey or black above with a yellowish belly and lacks a distinct neck. It features a compressed, paddle-like tail and small, non-overlapping scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis obscurus* is best distinguished by its 29–35 scale rows around the neck and a distinctively small, narrow head, which is significantly slenderer than its body.
ai.habitat: *Hydrophis obscurus* inhabits the coastal waters, estuaries, and mangrove forests of the Indian subcontinent, typically remaining in shallow, muddy-bottomed marine areas.
ai.behavior: Russell's sea snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small fish and crustaceans along coastal waters and muddy estuaries under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis obscurus* is viviparous, producing litters of 3–15 young. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed between March and July in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hydrophis obscurus* occurs along the coastal waters of India, primarily from the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Islands to the western coast of the Indian subcontinent.
